name: Connections reform timeline
fact: NESO's revised 2026-27 timetable phases protected, Gate 2 Phase 1 and Gate 2 Phase 2 offers, with final distribution batches extending to March 2027.
gate: A published programme window is not a site-specific energisation date or capacity reservation.

name: Connections offer transparency update
fact: NESO reported first protected Gate 2 offers progressing and noted distribution offers are developed separately by DNOs.
gate: Cross-industry offer progress must not be transferred to a specific site's status.

name: Connections offers June 2026 milestone
fact: As of 10 June 2026 NESO and electricity networks reported 713 of 1,223 pre-2030 pipeline projects had received offers, representing 37GW.
gate: An aggregate offer milestone is not proof a target development has an offer, reserved headroom or energisation date.

name: Connections Reform overview
fact: NESO's reform hub publishes the current delivery pipeline, reform timeline, EA register and customer resources.
gate: Reform-hub presence is context, not project-specific connection evidence.

name: Connections Reform results
fact: NESO publishes pipeline and zonal reform results and warns contextual RESP mapping does not replace operational connection zones or customer progression data.
gate: Zonal capacity/result maps must not be used as a confirmed project connection point or current customer status.

name: About Connections Reform
fact: NESO explains Gate 1 and Gate 2: Gate 2 can secure a confirmed connection date, point and queue position, while Gate 1 does not.
gate: Gate 2 criteria/status still requires exact project evidence; regional capacity cannot infer a site's Gate status.

name: Gate 1 information
fact: NESO states Gate 1 does not reserve capacity, a queue place, protected status or guarantee a connection.
gate: Never treat Gate 1 presence as connection capacity or an energisation commitment.

name: Connections Reform customer area
fact: NESO's customer area routes users to Gate 1 information, timelines, queue management, portals and offer-support material.
gate: Process resources do not establish a target site's connection status.

name: Transition to Connections Reform
fact: NESO documents the transition from paused applications into the reformed connections process and new gated modification approach.
gate: Historic transitional rules must not be applied as current project status without exact application dates.

name: Connections Offer Process legacy page
fact: NESO explicitly warns some information on this page is no longer current and directs users to Connections Reform for latest application-window information.
gate: A legacy process page cannot override current reform rules.

name: Ofgem demand connections reform update
fact: Ofgem's 16 June 2026 update says demand reform is addressing a large queue, non-viable projects and delays for well-progressed demand projects.
gate: Policy work is not a final site-specific demand connection decision.

name: Ofgem demand connections reform call for input
fact: Ofgem published its 2026 call for input and response summary, while stating emerging policy views should not be read as final decisions.
gate: Consultation analysis is not final connection policy or site approval.

name: Ofgem G2tWQ timetable decision
fact: Ofgem agreed a phased alternative timetable for G2tWQ offers, with batches across 2026 and final completion expected by mid-March 2027.
gate: Regulatory timetable approval is not a project-specific offer or energisation guarantee.

name: Ofgem connections reform and battery capacity update
fact: Ofgem published an April 2026 transparency update with DESNZ on reform progress and battery storage oversupply in the reformed queue.
gate: Technology-level queue context is not evidence of local network headroom.

name: UKPN Open Data Portal
fact: UK Power Networks' portal exposes network asset, capacity and utilisation datasets for planning and connection discovery.
gate: Open-data capacity is screening evidence and must not be treated as a formal connection offer.

name: UKPN capacity visibility
fact: UKPN describes GSP-level spare-capacity and queue visibility intended to improve siting decisions.
gate: Queue/headroom visibility is informative and does not reserve capacity for a new applicant.

name: UKPN pre-application support
fact: UKPN offers pre-application advice, open data, cable plans and Appendix G context before a formal connection application.
gate: Advice, network plans or Appendix G summaries do not constitute an accepted connection offer.

name: UKPN Major Connections plan
fact: UKPN's major-connections plan describes open data and future capacity visibility to support locational connection decisions.
gate: Strategic commitments and future-capacity indicators are not present-day reserved capacity.

name: UKPN data-centre connection products
fact: UKPN describes standard, ramped, flexible and profiled connection products for large demand customers including data centres.
gate: Product availability does not prove eligibility, capacity, cost or timing for a specific site.

name: UKPN connections products
fact: UKPN publishes standard, timed/profiled, DERMS-curtailed and ramped connection products.
gate: A flexible/ramped option changes contractual capacity behaviour and must not be treated as firm full-capacity headroom.

name: UKPN connections business
fact: UKPN describes its connections operations and use of DERMS to enable customers in constrained areas.
gate: Operational capability at network level is not a site-specific connection decision.

name: UKPN DER helpful resources
fact: UKPN links current connection guidance, the 2026 ENA DG guide, Embedded Capacity Register and approximate Network Infrastructure and Usage map.
gate: A map or guide is discovery/context evidence, not an accepted G99/G100 connection.

name: UKPN flexible connections
fact: UKPN explains flexible DER connections can avoid reinforcement by accepting export curtailment managed by DERMS.
gate: A flexible connection is non-firm and must not be scored as unrestricted firm capacity.

name: UKPN profiled connection
fact: UKPN's profiled connection varies maximum demand by time window and can include a guaranteed minimum plus flexible extra capacity.
gate: Maximum profile capacity must not be treated as continuously available firm demand capacity.

name: NGED network capacity map
fact: NGED says its network-capacity map indicates where large-scale development may connect with less reinforcement and explicitly does not replace a formal application.
gate: Map colour/headroom is indicative and can change as quotations are issued or expire.
